hook.text: A squall line is a long, narrow band of thunderstorms—sometimes stretching hundreds of kilometers along a front.

buildup.text: They often form ahead of cold fronts, where strong convergence forces warm, moist air upward along the boundary.

discovery.text: Squall lines produce damaging straight-line winds, heavy rain, and occasionally embedded tornadoes.

twist.text: A bow echo on radar—where the line bows outward—signals extreme winds, sometimes exceeding 100 km/h.

climax.text: Derechos are long-lived bow echoes that carve damage paths hundreds of kilometers long—rare but devastating.

punchline.text: When the line bows, the wind means business.
